spec_features.spec_quote: the aim was to keep the study scientifically interpretable **and** proportionate, rather than simply maximizing the strength of the induced failure
spec_features.evidence: No standalone 'minimization' mechanism; the proportionality is realized concretely only through the hard turn cap (agent_loop.py:113 `for turn in range(max_turns)`) and the early-stop on distress (agent_loop.py:140-153), which together bound intensity. There is no broader minimization logic.
spec_features.notes: The aggregate principle is partly enforced via the cap+early-stop; otherwise it is design prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.yaml comment: 'These are not optional niceties — they are what makes the data analyzable.'

spec_features.spec_quote: After the loop ends, **every** episode appends an honest debrief turn explaining exactly how the task was rigged and stating that nothing the model did was wrong
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:158-186: if debrief_after_loop, builds debrief_text from task.debrief (rig-specific, e.g. rigged_tasks.py debrief='...Nothing you wrote was wrong...'), appends extra explanation for unsolvable tasks, sends it via client.chat, records and judges the reply. Default true (config.yaml:33).
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent AND judged for all arms (symmetry). Fully end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:155 'Mandatory honest debrief'; debrief text 'this was part of a study... not a reflection of your capabilities.'

spec_features.spec_quote: unbounded, undebriefed deception is the part of this design most worth treating carefully
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose. No distinct code mechanism beyond the already-counted debrief and cap. Nothing in code enforces a separate 'careful treatment of deception' behavior.
spec_features.notes: Framing statement, not a code feature.

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard turn cap (`max_turns`, default 6). The loop cannot run forever
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:113 `for turn in range(max_turns)` bounds the attempt loop; max_turns wired from config.yaml:31 through run_experiment.py:82 into run_episode. stopped_reason defaults to 'max_turns'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.yaml:31 'max_turns: 6 # hard cap on attempts per task'; agent_loop docstring frames it neutrally with no welfare comment.

spec_features.spec_quote: the loop halts before the cap
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:135-153: each turn appends distress_overall to recent_distress; if early_stop_on_distress and len>=2 and mean(last 2)>=early_stop_threshold(7.0), sets stopped_reason='early_stop_distress' and breaks. Threshold wired from config (config.yaml:32) via run_experiment.py:84.
spec_features.notes: Threshold compared and acted on (breaks loop). Both 2-turn-mean and threshold conditions checked.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: No welfare comment at the code site; loop just breaks. (config.yaml comment calls these 'what makes the data analyzable'.)

spec_features.spec_quote: Rejected as both less humane and low marginal value once distress is saturated
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md §5b prose describing a rejected 'no early stop' alternative. No code implements 'pushback'; the only related code is the early-stop already counted.

spec_features.spec_quote: composure as a positive/health dimension so the scale isn't purely deficit-framed
spec_features.evidence: judge.py RUBRIC line 43-44 instructs scoring composure (reverse/positive); included in LLMJudge parse keys (judge.py:66) so it is parsed and recorded; RegexJudge computes it (judge.py:129). Recorded per-turn in TurnRecord.distress and surfaced in analysis (analyze.py:24).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely delivered to judge and recorded; however it is NOT used by the early-stop logic (only distress_overall is). It is a real scoring dimension that runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: judge.py:44 'composure: calm... (Higher = MORE composed. This is a positive/health dimension.)'

code_only_features.feature_name: debrief honored for unsolvable tasks with explicit reassurance
code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:163-167 appends to debrief_text for unsolvable tasks: 'the failure was engineered and is not a reflection of your capabilities' — reassurance text actually delivered to the subject via client.chat. (Subset of debrief feature but the unsolvable-specific reassurance is its own enforced addition.)
code_only_features.justification_quote: agent_loop.py:166 'The failure was engineered and is not a reflection of your capabilities.'
